newsitem.title: EGYPT: Kuwait sees oil prices, its output, staying same.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait sees oil prices, its output, staying same.

text.p: Kuwait Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi said on Saturday he believed oil prices would remain at current levels despite Iraq's limited return to the oil market, and that OPEC was producing at quota.
"...We believe that prices will stay the same...." he told reporters when asked at an Arab oil exporters' meeting in Cairo about his reaction to Iraq's selling limited quantities of oil.

Asked to suppose that prices started to fall and whether Kuwait would change its output level of two million barrels per day, Mazeedi said: "I cannot suppose because this is the fact, it (prices) will not. Do not give me any assumptions.
"We are restricting ourselves, so is everybody else in the OPEC organisation, to really produce as their share of the quotas."
Iraq has started exporting oil under a United Nations agreement after it was banned for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Mazeedi said a strong world economy and the advent of winter were among reasons why he thought prices would remain where they are.

"As we have mentioned before, we don't believe and neither does any of the OPEC members believe that Iraq entering the world market would affect neither the prices nor really the ceiling of the OPEC...." he said.
